insuranceMethodology.profile: Published March 2026 reference: 34-year-old male, Alderley Brisbane, clean record, garaged, 15,000km/year, market value, about A$900 excess; entry variants.
insuranceMethodology.interpretation: Prefer a recent exact-model benchmark over a generic class proxy. Brisbane entry-variant quote studies, national single-insurer sold-policy aggregates and a NSW annualised study have different populations; do not pool their means. A published range midpoint is a planning choice, not an observed mean. Youi describes its indicative range as covering 80% of applicable premiums within or below it, not a confidence interval. None is a household quote; bounds and proxy adjustments remain assumptions.
insuranceMethodology.rangeMeaning: Illustrative household-budget sensitivity range. Actual premiums can fall outside it, especially with young drivers, claims, different parking/address, excess or cover.

tyresAnnual.basis: At 15,000km/year: point = A$1,600 fitted set × 15,000/40,000km. Low = A$1,200 × 15,000/50,000; high = A$2,400 × 15,000/30,000. Set prices and service lives are planning assumptions anchored to current fitted SUV-tyre retail prices, not model-specific quotes or guaranteed tyre life. Larger/staggered wheels can cost more; use the correct size and load rating.
tyresAnnual.note: An accrual for eventual replacement, not an assertion that four tyres are purchased every year. Fitting/balancing are included in the reference retail prices; additional alignment/repair costs are separate.

charger.basis: All-in standard-home planning budget: A$800 Wall Connector hardware + EVSE’s typical Brisbane installation A$1,000–1,500. Midpoint A$800 + A$1,250 = A$2,050. This combines two published references, not an installation quote or bundled offer. Assumes suitable existing electrical supply, straightforward cable route and no major switchboard/strata/civil works. Set to zero if already equipped or not needed.
charger.note: Not all chargers, homes or cars need the same setup. Confirm compatible connector, AC charging limit, hardware availability, GST/inclusions and site quote. Complex works can exceed this range; no rebate assumed.

inspection.basis: Default A$385 is RACQ Premium Inspection non-member pricing. Mechanical inspection is A$315 member/A$340 non-member; Premium is A$360/A$385. A$680 upper planning option combines A$385 Premium + A$295 mobile EV battery check. The range spans different inclusions, not varying prices for the same inspection. No safety-certificate add-on included.

evBatteryCheck.basis: Optional RACQ battery-health diagnostic: in-store member/non-member A$200/A$225; mobile A$270/A$295. Confirm model compatibility and location. Separate from mechanical/body inspection.

inspection.note: Add the optional battery check only when selected; do not add it twice or assume a generic inspection establishes traction-battery health.

BEV.basis: Dashboard planning assumption: 15% annual reducing-balance loss, with 8–25% sensitivity. AADA documents BEV resale pressure from price cuts; it does not publish these forecast rates. Apply from today’s purchase price, not original MSRP. Age, model, new-car prices and condition can overwhelm the class assumption.

PHEV.basis: Dashboard planning assumption: 12% annual reducing-balance loss, with 7–20% sensitivity. Intermediate scenario reflecting AADA’s mixed PHEV resale picture; no claimed measured annual rate or resale guarantee. Apply to today’s purchase price and allow an owner-entered resale override.

HEV.basis: Dashboard planning assumption: 10% annual reducing-balance loss, with 5–16% sensitivity. AADA reports stronger recent hybrid retention, which supports a lower-loss scenario direction, not these exact rates. Exceptional historical prices are not projected as future appreciation.

PETROL.basis: Planning assumption: 12% annual reducing-balance loss, with 5–20% sensitivity. This is an editable scenario, not a measured forecast for this fuel or model. Apply to today’s purchase price. Age, supply, condition, mileage and new-car prices can outweigh the powertrain assumption.

DIESEL.basis: Planning assumption: 12% annual reducing-balance loss, with 5–20% sensitivity. This is an editable scenario, not a measured forecast for this fuel or model. Apply to today’s purchase price. Age, supply, condition, mileage and new-car prices can outweigh the powertrain assumption.

depreciationMethodology.note: Low rate means less depreciation and higher retained value. Model economic depreciation as purchase less resale; do not double-count purchase principal and depreciation in ownership cost. These are scenario assumptions, not predicted transaction prices or confidence intervals.

displayNote: All estimates, proxy adjustments, assumed bounds and future resale scenarios should carry the dashboard’s yellow estimate styling. Published supplier or research anchors do not make a personal projection certain.
